'''Jelena Vučković''' is a Serbian-born American scientist, and a Jensen Huang Professor of Global Leadership, Professor of Electrical Engineering, and by courtesy of Applied Physics at Stanford University.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://web.stanford.edu/dept/app-physics/cgi-bin/faculty/ |title = Stanford University Department of Applied Physics » Faculty}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.stanford.edu/people/jelena-vuckovic|title=Stanford School of Engineering Faculty |language=en}}</ref> She served as Fortinet Founders Chair of the Department of Electrical Engineering at [[Stanford University]] from August 2021 through June 2023.<ref name="Jelena Vuckovic - CV">{{Cite web|title=Jelena Vuckovic - CV|url=https://web.stanford.edu/~jela/|access-date=2024-03-07|language=en}}</ref> Vučković leads the Nanoscale and Quantum Photonics (NQP) Lab, and is a faculty member of the Ginzton Lab, PULSE Institute, SIMES Institute, and Bio-X at Stanford. She was the inaugural director of the Q-FARM initiative (Quantum Fundamentals, ARchitecture and Machines).<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://news.stanford.edu/2019/02/08/q-farm-initiative-bolster-quantum-research-stanford-slac/ |title = Q-FARM initiative bolsters quantum research at Stanford-SLAC|date = 2019-02-08}}</ref> She is a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], an External Scientific Member<ref name="Jelena Vučković appointed at MPQ as new External Scientific Member">{{Cite web|title=Jelena Vučković appointed at MPQ as new External Scientific Member |url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/jelena-vuckovic |access-date=2025-02-25|language=en}}</ref> of the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]], and a Fellow of [[The Optical Society]], the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].

Vučković's research interests include [[nanophotonics]], [[quantum information]] technologies, [[quantum optics]], [[photonics]] inverse design, [[nonlinear optics]], [[optoelectronics]], [[cavity QED]].<ref name="stanford.edu">{{Cite web | url=https://stanford.edu/~jela/ |title = Jelena Vuckovic, Professor at Stanford University}}</ref><ref name="biox.stanford.edu">{{Cite web | url=https://biox.stanford.edu/about/people/affiliated-faculty/jelena-vuckovic-professor-electrical-engineering |title = Jelena Vuckovic - Professor of Electrical Engineering|date = 2014-06-20}}</ref>

Vučković is the Lead editor for Physical Review Applied.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editors of Physical Review Applied|url=https://journals.aps.org/prapplied/staff|access-date=2025-02-25|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Physical Review Applied |doi=10.1103/PhysRevApplied.22.050001 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prapplied/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevApplied.22.050001|access-date=2025-02-25|language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Jelena Vučković was born in [[Niš, Serbia]]. Her father was a high school professor. Her mother worked in sales for a big glass factory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shell |first=Lea |title=Before They Were Scientists: Jelena Vuckovic |url=https://yourwildlife.org/2014/09/before-they-were-scientists-jelena-vuckovic/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=Your Wild Life |language=en-US}}</ref>  She studied at the [[University of Nis|University of Niš]], where she also worked as a Teaching Assistant for two years before moving to Australia.<ref name="ee.caltech.edu">{{cite web |title=Electrical Engineering :: Centennial |url=http://ee.caltech.edu/centennial/speakers/vuckovic.html |website=ee.caltech.edu |access-date=4 February 2020}}</ref> She received her M.S. (1997) and PhD (2002) in Electrical Engineering from the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech). In 2002, she was a postdoctoral scholar in the Applied Physics Department at Stanford. She became Assistant Professor in the Electrical Engineering Department in 2003.<ref name="JV-profileSU">{{cite web | url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/jelena-vuckovic | title=Jelena Vuckovic's Profile &#124; Stanford Profiles }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Vučković is the Jensen Huang Professor in Global Leadership, Professor of Electrical Engineering, and by courtesy of Applied Physics at Stanford University. She is the lead/principal investigator the NQP Lab at Stanford, and is a faculty member of the Ginzton Lab, PULSE, SPRC, SystemX, and Bio-X.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nqp.stanford.edu/|title=Nanoscale and Quantum Photonics Lab|website=nqp.stanford.edu}}</ref><ref name="JV-profileSU" />

Her PhD advisees include [[Ilya Fushman]] (PhD 2008),<ref name="JV-AcademicTree">{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/etree/tree.php?pid=178225|title = E-Tree - Jelena Vuckovic Family Tree}}</ref> and she and Fushman were among lead authors on a [[quantum computing]] paper published in ''[[Nature (magazine)|Nature]]'' in 2007<ref name="06_12_2007_nature.com">{{Citation|date=25 January 2023|title=Controlling cavity reflectivity with a single quantum dot|newspaper=[[Nature (magazine)|Nature]]|doi=10.1038/nature06234 |url= https://www.nature.com/articles/nature06234|access-date=26 January 2023 |last1=Englund |first1=Dirk |last2=Faraon |first2=Andrei |last3=Fushman |first3=Ilya |last4=Stoltz |first4=Nick |last5=Petroff |first5=Pierre |last6=Vučković |first6=Jelena |volume=450 |issue=7171 |pages=857–861 |pmid=18064008 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and ''[[Science (magazine)|Science]]'' in 2008.<ref name="09_05_2008_pubmed.com">{{Citation|last=Fushman|first=Ilya|date=9 May 2008|title=Controlled phase shifts with a single quantum dot|journal=Science|volume=320 |issue=5877 |pages=769–772 |doi=10.1126/science.1154643 |pmid=18467584 |s2cid=1119777 }}</ref>

Other PhD advisees include Andrei Faraon (PhD 2009),<ref name="2009_caltech.edu">{{Citation|year=2009 |title=Andrew Faraon|publisher=Caltech|url=http://www.its.caltech.edu/~faraon/|access-date=25 January 2023}}</ref><ref name="JV-AcademicTree" /> MIT professor Dirk Englund (PhD 2008),<ref name="2008_mit.edu">{{Citation |year=2008 |title=Dirk Englund |publisher=MIT |url=http://www.rle.mit.edu/qp/people/ |access-date=25 January 2023}}</ref> Harvard professor Kiyoul Yang, and [[Hatice Altug]] (PhD 2006), professor at the [[Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne]].<ref name="2006_epfl.ch">{{Citation|year=2006|title=Dirk Englund|publisher=EPFL|url=https://bios.epfl.ch/people|access-date=25 January 2023}}</ref>

{{As of|2018}}, Vuckovic's research areas include:<ref name="stanford.edu"/><ref name="biox.stanford.edu"/> [[nanophotonics]], [[quantum information]], [[quantum technology]], [[quantum optics]], [[Integrated quantum photonics]], [[photonics]] inverse design, [[nonlinear optics]], [[optoelectronics]], and [[cavity QED]].

Vučković's lab invented a software suite called Spins.<ref name="techfinder.stanford.edu">{{Cite web | url=https://techfinder.stanford.edu/technology/spins-inverse-design-software-nanophotonic-structures | title=Stanford University Explore Technologies | access-date=2024-03-08 | archive-date=2024-07-26 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240726123256/https://techfinder.stanford.edu/technology/spins-inverse-design-software-nanophotonic-structures | url-status=dead }}</ref> Spins automates the design of arbitrary nanophotonic devices by leveraging gradient-based optimization techniques that can explore a large space of possible designs. The resulting devices have higher efficiencies, smaller footprints, and novel functionalities.,<ref name="techfinder.stanford.edu"/> Vuckovic is a cofounder and an advisory board member of Spins Photonics Inc, the company commercializing photonics inverse design.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spinsphotonics.com/|title=Spins Photonics.com}}</ref> Vučković holds 20 patents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/search?q=jelena+vuckovic|title=Search Patents - Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref>

Vučković was the "Fortinet Founders" chair of the [[Stanford Department of Electrical Engineering]] from August 2021 – June 2023,<ref name="Jelena Vuckovic - CV"/> and lead researcher of the Nanoscale and Quantum Photonics (NQP) lab.<ref name="26_01_2023_/web.stanford.edu/~jela">{{Citation|date=25 January 2023|title=Jelena Vuckovic|publisher=Stanford University|url=http://web.stanford.edu/~jela/|access-date=25 January 2023}}</ref>
